# A page cannot take itself off screen, and closing a tab is not reported to
# it reliably, so on html a window's `visible` and `@closed` mean nothing --
# and each is refused at the window rather than emitted and ignored, which is
# what html did before. The literal default, `visible=true`, says nothing and
# builds. gtk4 builds all of it.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html bound.sngl
stderr 'bound.sngl:5:16: html cannot show or hide a window, so its `visible` cannot be bound'

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html2 hidden.sngl
stderr 'hidden.sngl:3:16: html cannot show or hide a window, so its `visible` is always true'

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html3 closed.sngl
stderr 'closed.sngl:5:16: html reports no close of a window, so its `@closed` would never run'

sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o html4 default.sngl

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 bound.sngl
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4b closed.sngl

-- bound.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var shown = true

ui.window #main(title="Main", :visible=shown) {
    ui.text(value="main")
}
-- hidden.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

ui.window #main(title="Main", visible=false) {
    ui.text(value="main")
}
-- closed.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

var closes = 0

ui.window #main(title="Main", @closed {
    closes += 1
}) {
    ui.text(value="{closes}")
}
-- default.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

ui.window #main(title="Main", visible=true) {
    ui.text(value="main")
}
